font-pairing-hierarchy-decision.label: Browse Free Fonts
font-pairing-hierarchy-decision.note: Every family page sets each style it ships in your own text, at body and display sizes — the weight check from section 6.

font-pairing-hierarchy-decision.label: PT Sans
font-pairing-hierarchy-decision.note: The sans half of the PT superfamily named in section 5. Its page suggests PT Serif for body text.

font-pairing-hierarchy-decision.label: PT Serif
font-pairing-hierarchy-decision.note: The serif half of the same superfamily. Its page pairs it with PT Sans for UI text and PT Mono as the monospace.

type-scale-systems.label: Browse Free Fonts
type-scale-systems.note: Filter by Sans Serif, Serif, Display or Monospace to find the body, heading and code faces section 7 describes.

color-contrast-systems.label: Browse Color Palettes
color-contrast-systems.note: Ready-made four-color palettes for practicing the section 9 audit: check each text-and-background pairing against 4.5:1.

color-contrast-systems.label: Open the Color Library
color-contrast-systems.note: When a pairing fails, look through the other shades in that color's family for a lighter or darker neighbor, then check it again.

color-palette-token-system.label: Try the Image Picker
color-palette-token-system.note: Pull starting colors from a photo and copy them as CSS custom properties — raw values for the primitive tier in section 4.

color-palette-token-system.label: Browse Color Palettes
color-palette-token-system.note: Four named colors to start from. Section 3 shows how to turn each hue into a tonal ramp.
